statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-11850 is an integer underflow and heap read overrun in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB module (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c), reached when an LDAP server returns a krbExtraData attribute shorter than 2 bytes to the KDC or kadmind. MIT added the length check in commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2a5fd83d4436583f2ddc0e193269a4d800ee45c4 (ticket 9206, https://krbdev.mit.edu/rt/Ticket/Display.html?id=9206) and released it in krb5 1.22.3 (https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/974a8875767a2f375669f84b176c7d98a7c85a20 on the 1.22 branch); its message says the impact is negligible because the attacker would have to control the KDB LDAP server. This owner is based on Debian's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1, which lacks the check (Debian marks trixie vulnerable with urgency unimportant: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11850), and every published build ships the LDAP KDB module in krb5-kdc-ldap. Pending: a decision whether to backport the upstream check or to record MIT's trust-boundary reasoning; Red Hat rates this Moderate and has issued a fix in RHSA-2026:25520 (https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-11850), so a not-affected statement needs a recorded maintainer decision.
